title: Balloon Lavender Lesson
subject: A striped hot air balloon floating over a lavender field at sunset, with purple hills, a golden hill, and a lone tree on the right.

steps.name: Paint the sunset sky
steps.summary: Blend the sunset sky from blue at the top to orange, with a gold glow.

paints.name: Sky blue
paints.recipe: 3 parts white, 2 parts ultramarine, a touch of burnt sienna

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

paints.name: Sunset gold
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 2 parts red, 2 parts white

do: Load the 1 inch flat with Sky blue and paint long side-to-side strokes across the top tenth of the canvas.
Below the blue, paint Sunset orange in long strokes, blending up into the blue while both are wet so it turns a soft violet where they meet.
Brush Sunset gold in a wide oval glow a little left of center, a bit below the middle of the sky, and blend its edges into the orange.
Keep the orange going down to about 6/10 of the way down the canvas, with a straight bottom edge. Leave the bottom 4/10 white.
watch_out: Stopping the sky at the hill line. Run it lower; the mountains and fields cover it later.
Overworking the blend until it's muddy. A few passes are enough.

steps.name: Dab in the big clouds
steps.summary: Scrub in the big pink cloud masses and their orange undersides.

paints.name: Coral pink
paints.recipe: 3 parts red, 2 parts white, 1 part ultramarine

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

paints.name: Peach light
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 3 parts yellow, 2 parts red, 1 part burnt sienna

brushes.use: scrubbing in the cloud masses and streaks

do: With the filbert and Coral pink, scrub in a big cloud mass over the upper right, from the middle of the canvas to the right edge and from the top down to about a third.
Scrub a smaller pink cloud group on the upper left, from the left edge to about a fifth across, and leave the blue showing in the top middle.
Drag a few long, thin pink-orange streaks across the sky below the clouds, down to just above the glow.
Dab Peach light on the tops of the cloud masses, where the sun lights them.
watch_out: Making lots of small separate puffs. Keep the clouds as two big masses and a few streaks.
Covering the gold glow. Keep the streaks thin near the middle so the glow stays bright.

steps.name: Paint the sun
steps.summary: Paint the small, bright sun inside the glow.

paints.name: Sun cream
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 3 parts yellow, 1 part red

do: Load the #6 round with Sun cream and paint a small solid circle in the brightest part of the glow, a little left of center and about 4/10 of the way down.
Make it about one-twenty-fifth of the canvas width across.
With a dry, clean brush, lightly soften the edge so it glows into the gold.
watch_out: Making the sun too big. It's only about the width of a fingertip on a 16 x 24 inch canvas.
Thin paint. Use it thick so the orange doesn't show through.

steps.name: Paint the far mountains
steps.summary: Lay the far purple mountains across the whole width.

paints.name: Mountain purple
paints.recipe: 1 part ultramarine, 1 part white, a touch of red

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

do: Paint the far mountains in Mountain purple across the whole width: a rounded peak on the left about 4/10 down, dipping down right over the bottom half of the sun.
Rise again to a second ridge right of center, and keep the ridge going at about the same height to the right edge.
Fill the mountains down to about half way down the canvas.
Blend a little Sunset orange into the purple near the sun, where the glow lights the slopes. The orange sky still shows below the mountains.
watch_out: Hard, sharp ridge lines. Far mountains look softer and lighter than near ones.
Leaving the whole sun showing. The ridge dips over its lower half, so it looks like it's setting.

steps.name: Paint the golden fields and hill
steps.summary: Add the golden fields and hill under the mountains.

paints.name: Field gold
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 1 part red, a touch of ultramarine

paints.name: Sunset orange
paints.recipe: 2 parts red, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

brushes.use: the field band and the hill

do: Paint a band of Field gold across the left half, just under the mountains, about half way down the canvas.
Paint the big golden hill on the right: start low near the left third and sweep it up to the right edge, where its top is just below the mountains.
Run the gold down to a straight edge a little more than 6/10 of the way down everywhere, past where the lavender will start.
Drag a little Sunset orange along the lower slope of the hill for a warm shadow.
watch_out: Stopping right at the lavender line. Run the gold a little lower; the lavender covers it.
Flat, even gold. Let some orange and lighter gold strokes show so the hill looks like grass.

steps.name: Dab the tree lines
steps.summary: Dab in the dark tree lines along the foot of the mountains.

paints.name: Tree green
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, a touch of red, a touch of white

paints.name: Sunlit green
paints.recipe: 1 part yellow, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of ultramarine

brushes.use: the small bumps of the far row

do: Dab a thin row of small Tree green bumps along the bottom of the mountains, from the left edge to past the middle, so it ends against the golden hill.
Dab a nearer, taller row of rounded bushy bumps across the left half, along the bottom of the left field.
Touch a little Sunlit green on a few of the tops. Leave the golden hill on the right bare.
watch_out: Painting single trees. Keep it a bumpy row, not separate trees.
Making the far row as big as the near one. Farther away means smaller.

steps.name: Paint the lone tree
steps.summary: Pull up the tree on the right and dab its leafy crown.

paints.name: Trunk brown
paints.recipe: 2 parts ultramarine, 2 parts burnt sienna, 1 part red, a touch of white

paints.name: Tree green
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, a touch of red, a touch of white

do: Pull the trunk up from the top of the golden hill, near the right edge (about 85% across), in Trunk brown: wide at the base, then splitting into two or three branches.
Build the crown in Tree green as three or four overlapping round clusters of dabs: one on the left, a higher one in the middle, one on the right, and one along the bottom.
Make the crown about half again as wide as it is tall, reaching up to about a fifth of the way down the canvas.
Leave a gap or two at the bottom of the crown where the branches show.
watch_out: A lollipop tree (a ball on a stick). Make the crown out of lumpy clusters, wider than tall.
A trunk as thick at the top as the bottom. Taper it as it rises.

steps.name: Block in the lavender rows and paths
steps.summary: Paint the lavender rows and the two paths, all running to one point.

paints.name: Path brown
paints.recipe: 2 parts burnt sienna, 1 part red, 1 part white

paints.name: Lavender dark
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part white, a touch of red, a touch of burnt sienna

brushes.use: the path edges and the narrow far rows

do: Find the spot where the two paths meet: at the top of the field, a little right of center (about 6/10 across).

From that spot, paint two Path brown paths down to the bottom edge: the left one landing a little left of center (about a third across), the right one landing near the right side (about 8/10 across). Each is a thin point at the top and a wide strip at the bottom.
Fill the row between the paths with Lavender dark, then the rows beside them: long dark bands that slant toward the meeting spot.
Make the rows thinner and closer together near the top of the field, and wide at the bottom. Cover all the white.
watch_out: Paths that stay the same width. They must narrow to a point near the top of the field.
Adding texture now. This step is flat dark purple; the dabs come next.

steps.name: Dab the lavender
steps.summary: Press short purple dabs along every row.

paints.name: Lavender mid
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 2 parts white, 1 part red

brushes.use: big dabs in the front rows
small dabs in the far rows

do: Load the filbert with Lavender mid and press short dabs along each row, pointing slightly upward, following the row's slant toward the meeting point.
In the front rows at the bottom of the canvas, make big dabs; in the far rows near the top of the field, make small ones.
Leave the bottom edge of each row dark so the rows look rounded.
Keep the paths brown; don't dab into them.
watch_out: Covering the dark base. The dark shows between the dabs and makes the rows look round.
Same-size dabs everywhere. Big in front, small at the back.

steps.name: Add light to the lavender
steps.summary: Tap light lavender on the row tops so they catch the sun.

paints.name: Lavender light
paints.recipe: 3 parts white, 2 parts ultramarine, 1 part red

do: Load the small filbert with Lavender light and tap it on the tops of the lavender rows, over the mid purple.
Put the most on the front rows at the bottom, and only a few small touches on the far rows.
Keep each row's dark bottom showing, so every row goes dark, then mid purple, then light on top.
watch_out: Light dabs on every part of every row. Keep them to the tops so the rows stay round.

steps.name: Paint the striped balloon
steps.summary: Sketch and block in the balloon, its stripes, and the basket.

paints.name: Balloon red
paints.recipe: 1 part red, a touch of ultramarine, a touch of white

paints.name: Balloon yellow
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 1 part red, 1 part white, a touch of burnt sienna

paints.name: Balloon teal
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part yellow, 1 part white

paints.name: Trunk brown
paints.recipe: 2 parts ultramarine, 2 parts burnt sienna, 1 part red, a touch of white

brushes.use: the outline and the wide stripes
the narrow edge stripes, basket, and ropes

do: In the upper left (its middle about 28% across), sketch the balloon lightly: a big circle for the top, tapering down to a short neck about a quarter of the way down the canvas. It's about as wide as it is tall.
Paint a teal stripe straight down the middle, from the top to the neck.
Paint the stripes on each side as curved bands, like ( ) around the middle one: yellow, then red at the edges. They get thinner as they curve around the sides.
Paint a small square basket in Trunk brown just below the neck, with a few thin lines up to the neck for ropes.
watch_out: Straight, parallel stripes. The stripes bend around the balloon, so the outer ones curve the most and get thin.
A round ball. The bottom narrows to a neck, like an upside-down teardrop.

steps.name: Final details and highlights
steps.summary: Finish the balloon's stripes and add the last highlights.

paints.name: Sunlit green
paints.recipe: 1 part yellow, 1 part burnt sienna, a touch of ultramarine

paints.name: Peach light
paints.recipe: 6 parts white, 3 parts yellow, 2 parts red, 1 part burnt sienna

paints.name: Lavender dark
paints.recipe: 3 parts ultramarine, 1 part white, a touch of red, a touch of burnt sienna

paints.name: Balloon yellow
paints.recipe: 3 parts yellow, 1 part red, 1 part white, a touch of burnt sienna

brushes.use: the edge stripes and balloon shading
the sunlit dabs on the crown

do: Add a teal stripe down each outer edge of the balloon and a thin orange-red stripe beside the right-hand yellow, so the stripes get narrower toward the sides.
Darken the balloon's left and right edges a little with Balloon teal and Lavender dark, and add a few lighter streaks down the middle of the stripes.
Tap Sunlit green on the left side and top of the tree's crown, where the sun hits it.
Step back and stop. Don't add light everywhere.
watch_out: Adding highlights everywhere. Keep them to the sunlit sides.
Fussing with the lavender. It's done; the last touches go on the balloon and tree.
